The study used crushed sunflower crop (CSC) with a fraction of 1-2 mm3.
Paraffin was added to the CSC in a volume ratio of 1:1.
The composite material was melted and mixed before being cut into sample sizes.
Three sample sizes were used: 28 × 12 × 25, 23 × 10 × 45, and 28 × 12 × 5 mm.
Two waveguide techniques were used: P2-59 in a frequency range of 5.6 to 8.3 GHz and P2-61 in a frequency range of 8.15 to 12.1 GHz.
A metallic plate was used as a perfect reflector to measure reflection loss and transmittance.
The sample with a 25 mm thickness exhibited low reflection loss and high attenuation.
The air gap between the sample and reflector affected the behavior of the electromagnetic radiation.
The maximum absorption property observed was 20-30% with a frequency of the electromagnetic wave in the range 5.6-8.3 GHz.
Increasing the EMI frequency range increased transmittance and decreased the reflection coefficient.
The study was funded by the Russian Foundation for Basic Research and the government of the region of the Russian Federation.
The study aimed to understand the material's behavior under different conditions, including varying frequencies and sample positions.
The results showed that the material exhibits absorption properties depending on its geometrical size, position, and electromagnetic radiation frequency.
The study has implications for the design of high-performance microwave treatment chambers.
